text:
maya: Heads-up — since the rolling yesterday we've got several racks in eu-west1 with 1-2 long-running pods effectively pinning all GPUs. New batch jobs are stuck Pending. Anyone else seeing GPU islands?
jon: yep spotted. pods with podAntiAffinity rules + nodeSelector:gpu-type=ampere are forming tiny islands. scheduler can't pack around them.
leo: looks like many of those pods also have a taint tolerated: gpu.dedicated=training:NoSchedule — they're sticky.
anuj: can you paste one of the Pending pod events? also which nodes are affected?
maya: here —
maya: kubectl describe pod ml-batch-42 -n ml | sed -n '1,120p'
maya: Events:
  Type    Reason       Age   From               Message
  ----    ------       ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled    10m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ml/ml-batch-42 to node-gpu-eu-west1-a-12
  Warning FailedMount  9m    kubelet            MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "local-cache" : node affinity mismatch
jon: interesting — local-cache PV binding is preventing eviction/relocation, so even if we preempt, volume affinity blocks reschedule.
sam: this explains why pods linger and take whole node. storage affinity + NoSchedule taint = islanding.
descheduler-bot: recommended strategy: RemoveDuplicates + LowNodeUtilization; target pods older than 48h, consider ignoring pods with local PVs.
leo: I ran a quick query: kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.spec.tolerations)]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.metadata.namespace}{"\n"}{end}' | grep training — returns ~18 pods across 6 nodes.
anuj: TLDR: combination of (1) podAntiAffinity, (2) dedicated taints, (3) local PVs, and (4) high priority on some jobs. Scheduler won't preempt because preempting would break locality / storage constraints.
maya: ops asks: do we relax podAntiAffinity defaults for batch queue? that might allow binpacking.
jon: short-term: run descheduler in a controlled mode to evict duplicates / low-util pods that don't own local PVs. long-term: we should (a) add nodeAffinity that prefers not to leave single-pod-per-node for low-priority batch, (b) teach the autoscaler to prefer draining into warm nodes.
sam: cost note — Dedicated pool is underutilized on several AZs while others stuck at 90%. Spot and reserved counts mismatch causing us to spin extra capacity in other regions. RL cost already trending +9% this week.
leo: proposed plan:
  - run descheduler RemoveDuplicates on staging for 2 hours (will not touch pods with local PV label: "local-cache")
  - add a canary scheduler-policy tweak: decrease podAntiAffinity hard requirement to preferred for batch-* jobs
  - schedule a node label rollout: label some nodes as batch-consolidatable (batch=true)
  - monitor eviction rate and job latency
anuj: +1. Also add a k8s admission webhook to auto-convert strict requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity to preferred for jobs in the "batch" queue.
maya: can we get ownership from infra to run canary descheduler tonight at 2300 UTC? I'll hold a blameless runbook.
jon: I can run it and watch metrics. command I plan to run:
  kubectl run descheduler-canary -n kube-system --image=descheduler:latest --restart=Never -- \
    --policy-config-file=/policies/remove_duplicates_with_exceptions.yaml --dry-run=false
sam: add a metric alert: if PodPreemptionRate > 5/min or PendingJobsQueue > 200 for >10m then rollback.
descheduler-bot: note: descheduler will not evict pods with local PV annotation 'local-cache=true' in the canary policy file.
leo: one more: network observation — a couple of nodes show higher inter-pod latency when we try to pack two heavy GPU pods (nvlink saturation), so binpacking can introduce perf regressions. we'll need a perf test before we fully relax packing.
maya: agreed. timeline: canary descheduler tonight, perf microbench tomorrow AM, and if green, policy roll next week.
jon: I'll open a short runbook in #release-war-room and post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — also cc'ing cost to track the committed capacity impact. :money_with_wings:
maya: update: reserved capacity spike alert from billing just came in, will share graphs in 10m.
jon: cool. thanks all!
